claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 typically requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Adding a minor amount of SiC nanoparticles to ZrB2 powder enables densification below 2300 °C.
SiC nanoparticles promote formation of a transient eutectic liquid phase at particle interfaces during sintering.
The transient liquid phase enhances mass transport during sintering.
The transient liquid phase seals incipient pore sites.
Reduced porosity lowers the number of potential initiation sites for holes.
Reducing pore and hole initiation sites improves resistance to defects induced by liquid plating bath corrosion.
ZrB2 containing SiC nanoparticles and sintered below 2300 °C will have lower porosity than additive-free ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
ZrB2 containing SiC nanoparticles and sintered below 2300 °C will retain better structural integrity during prolonged liquid plating bath exposure than conventionally processed ZrB2.
The modified material will develop fewer holes and experience fewer failures during prolonged liquid plating bath exposure.

contradictions.description: The protocol says all processing variables or heating profiles are held constant except for SiC addition, but the control and modified samples are explicitly sintered in different temperature regimes (above versus below 2300 °C). Thus both composition and temperature vary, confounding attribution to the SiC intervention.
